sources.entry: Overleaf - Web-based collaborative LaTeX editor. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Ruby

summary.one_liner: Overleaf is an open-source, web-based, real-time collaborative LaTeX editor that can be self-hosted as the Community Edition.
summary.what_it_does: The repository holds the source code for Overleaf, an online collaborative LaTeX editor where multiple people can edit a project at the same time. The README describes a hosted version at overleaf.com and a self-hostable Community Edition. Installation is handled through a separate Overleaf Toolkit, which the README links to rather than documenting here. The repo includes two Dockerfiles: one builds a base image with dependencies such as wget and texlive, and the other builds the community image on top of it. Build targets are run from the server-ce directory via make. Services run inside a Phusion base image managed by the runit service manager. The README also mentions an enterprise offering, Overleaf Server Pro, with LDAP/SAML SSO and tracked changes, which is a separate paid product.
use_cases: write academic papers with co-authors in real time
run a local LaTeX editing server for a lab or workplace
compile LaTeX documents in the browser
contribute to an open-source online LaTeX editor
how_to_run: Installation instructions are in the Overleaf Toolkit (linked from the README; not included in this repo)
From server-ce/, run make build-base to build the base image
From server-ce/, run make build-community to build the community image
notable: Real-time multi-user editing of LaTeX projects
Official Docker images built from the repo (base image with texlive plus community image)
Sandbox Compiles option for isolating LaTeX compiles
Enterprise Server Pro edition adds SSO (LDAP/SAML) and tracked changes
caveats: Community Edition is only appropriate when all users are trusted; without Sandbox Compiles, users have full access to the container's filesystem, network and environment during compiles
Server Pro with SSO and tracked changes is a paid, officially supported product
The base image is heavy because it bundles texlive
